full_text_en:
Guo v. Company A, et al. — Dispute over Property Damage Compensation

Ruling Summary

1. Where a construction project does not entirely cover or occupy mineral resources but objectively renders all mineral resources within the mining right area incapable of being developed or utilized, it shall be deemed as complete coverage or occupation.

2. Where a railway construction project involving public interest has undergone the legally required procedures for approval of coverage or occupation of mineral resources, such coverage or occupation is not illegal and does not constitute infringement; a mining right holder who suffers losses as a result may seek compensation in accordance with law.

3. Compensation for coverage or occupation is based on the principle of compensating direct losses, and the scope of compensation includes direct losses such as the value of the mining right, the exploration investment apportioned to the covered mineral resources, investment in completed mining facilities, and expenses for relocating corresponding facilities. Where a party requests that the loss in mining right value be determined based on the mining right fee or transfer price payable under market conditions at the time of coverage for the covered mineral resource reserves, the people's court shall support such request.

4. The covered mineral resource reserves shall be determined based on the survey and assessment report relied upon by the natural resources authority in approving the coverage or the remaining mineral resource reserves that have been reviewed and filed with the natural resources authority. Where a mining right holder has on its own entrusted a relevant entity to prepare a mineral resource reserve survey or verification report that has not been submitted to the natural resources authority for review and filing in accordance with law, the people's court shall not accept such report.

Civil Judgment of the Supreme People's Court

(2024) Supreme People's Court Final Civil No. 28

Appellant (Original Defendant): Company A. Domicile: Xincheng District, Hohhot City, Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region.

Legal Representative: Chen, Chairperson of the Board.

Agent Ad Litem: Shi Zhezhi, Attorney at Tianjin Tianyuan Shitong Law Firm.

Appellant (Original Defendant): Company B. Domicile: Haidian District, Beijing City.

Legal Representative: Zhang, Chairperson of the Board.

Agent Ad Litem: Li Junjie, Attorney at Beijing Huixiang Law Firm.

Agent Ad Litem: Zhang Dongqing, Attorney at Beijing Huixiang Law Firm.

Respondent (Original Plaintiff): Guo, domiciled in Zunhua City, Hebei Province.

Agent Ad Litem: Yuan Song, Attorney at Tianjin Zonghui Law Firm.

Agent Ad Litem: Zhou Lemin, Attorney at Tianjin Zonghui Law Firm.

In the case of appeal by Company A and Company B against the respondent Guo concerning a dispute over property damage compensation, Company A and Company B, dissatisfied with the civil judgment of the Hebei High People's Court (2022) Hebei Civil First Instance No. 6, appealed to this Court. This Court, after accepting the case on January 25, 2024, formed a collegial panel in accordance with law and held a public hearing on March 1, 2024. The agent ad litem of appellant Company A, Shi Zhezhi; the agents ad litem of appellant Company B, Li Junjie and Zhang Dongqing; and the agents ad litem of respondent Guo, Yuan Song and Zhou Lemin, appeared before the court. The case has now been concluded.

Company A's grounds of appeal: 1. Set aside the judgment of first instance and amend to order that Company A compensate Guo for all losses totaling RMB 52,826,112 (including: mining right loss of RMB 276,900; shaft and tunnel loss of RMB 47,882,212; above-ground asset compensation value of RMB 3,044,300; and preliminary expenses and investment loss of RMB 1,622,700); 2. All litigation costs to be borne by Guo. Subsequently, Company A changed the first appeal request to: Set aside the judgment of first instance and amend to order that Company A compensate Mou Mining (now represented by Guo) for all losses totaling RMB 4,943,900, including mining right loss of RMB 276,900, above-ground asset compensation value of RMB 3,044,300, and preliminary expenses and investment loss of RMB 1,622,700. Facts and grounds: (1) Regarding compensation for mining rights. A. The judgment of first instance confused the concepts of mineral resource reserves and mineral resource quantities. According to the Mineral Resources Law of the PRC, the Measures for the Administration of Mineral Resource Registration and Statistics, and other relevant laws and regulations, mineral resources belong to the state, and mineral resource reserves and mineral resource quantities are two distinct concepts. In this case, the "Report on Verification of Mineral Resource Reserves of a Certain Iron Mine in Hebei Province" (hereinafter referred to as the "Reserve Verification Report" by Mou Geological Survey Institute) commissioned by Mou Mining in 2010, because it was not submitted to the competent natural resources authority for review and filing, the "resource reserves" in that report were in fact mineral resource quantities. The portion exceeding the reserves recorded in Mou Mining's mining license had not been applied for as a mining right from the state, nor had any corresponding fee or royalty been paid to the state. Company A is not legally obligated to compensate Mou Mining for this portion of newly increased mineral resource quantities. B. Mou Mining's further exploration of mineral resources within the original mining area constituted illegal exploration. The reserve verification report commissioned by Mou Mining (Guo) based on illegal exploration is itself illegal and should not be protected by law. Even if Company A were to compensate Mou Mining for the mining right, it should be based on the "Geological Report on Verification of Mineral Resource Reserves of a Certain Iron Mine in Zunhua City, Hebei Province" prepared by the Second Geological Brigade of the Hebei Bureau of Geology and Mineral Exploration and filed with the Tangshan Bureau of Land and Resources, with compensation for the mining right loss of RMB 276,900 based on the filed reserves of 64,100 tons. (2) Regarding compensation for underground asset losses such as shafts and tunnels. According to the "Notice of the Ministry of Land and Resources on Further Improving the Administration of Approval for Construction Projects Covering or Occupying Important Mineral Resources" (Guo Tu Zi Fa [2010] No. 137, hereinafter "Original Ministry of Land and Resources Document No. 137"), where the coverage area of a construction project overlaps with an exploration block or mining area but does not affect the normal exploration and extraction of mineral resources, it shall not be treated as coverage; where a construction project covers mineral resources with an established mining right, the scope of compensation shall in principle include: the exploration investment apportioned to the covered mineral resources, investment in completed mining facilities, and expenses for relocating corresponding facilities, i.e., direct losses. In this case, the Zhangjiakou-Tangshan Railway (hereinafter "Zhang-Tang Railway") project only covered part of Mou Mining's mining area and did not cover the filed reserves; in principle, it should not compensate Mou Mining for underground assets within the railway's coverage area. The "Geological Report on Verification of Mineral Resource Reserves of a Certain Iron Mine in Zunhua City, Hebei Province" filed with the Tangshan Bureau of Land and Resources recorded that there were two ore bodies within Mou Mining's mining area: ore body I-4 and ore body II. However, the "Development and Utilization Plan for Mineral Resources of a Certain Iron Mine in Zunhua City, Hebei Province" prepared by Company C in August 2007 and filed did not provide for the development and utilization of ore body II within Mou Mining's mining area. Therefore, the filed development and utilization plan cannot verify the utilization of shafts, tunnels, and other underground assets corresponding to ore body II. Based on page 3, section 1.1.3 of the "Development and Utilization Plan for Mineral Resources of Mou Mining" prepared by Company D in 2013, regarding external conditions for project construction and development status, it can be seen that ore body I-4 above -6 meters had been largely mined out; ore body II had previously been subjected to open-pit mining and later converted to underground mining, with corresponding underground mining facilities including wells No. 13, No. 14, inclined shaft J18, and adit No. 19. According to the "Retrospective Asset Valuation Report on Underground Asset Values Such as Shafts and Tunnels for Company A's Understanding" issued by a certain asset appraisal firm (special general partnership), the total asset value of these underground mining facilities was RMB 47,882,212. Therefore, even if compensation were to be made, it should be based on this amount. Other underground mining facilities, being in mined-out areas, having safety hazards, or having long been shut down, have no further value and should not be compensated. Alternatively, even if compensation were to be made for underground asset losses such as shafts and tunnels of Mou Mining within 1,000 meters on both sides of the Zhang-Tang Railway, the amount would be only RMB 91,159,894, not the RMB 146,789,700 determined in the first instance judgment. (3) Regarding compensation for preliminary expenses, investments, and business suspension losses. In this case, for the preliminary expenses, investments, and business suspension losses of Mou Mining and Zunhua City Mou Dressing Plant, according to the "Price Assessment Conclusion on Preliminary Expenses, Investments, and Business Suspension Losses of Mou Mining and Mou Dressing Plant" issued by Cangzhou Mou Price Appraisal Office commissioned by the court, among the assessed preliminary expenses, investments, and business suspension losses, apart from the land acquisition and tree compensation of RMB 7,486,100, the mining area preliminary investment of RMB 1,133,285, and the business suspension loss of RMB 16,079,850, which should not be compensated, the mining area preliminary expenses of RMB 1,043,100 and the mining area security personnel wages of RMB 579,600 are reasonable and may be compensated. The land acquisition and tree compensation for the mining area is relatively high and should be appropriately reduced as a cost based on the mining area's years of extraction. Other losses should not be compensated. (4) Regarding interest losses. The fundamental reason Mou Mining has not received compensation to date is not that Company A maliciously delayed or was at fault, but that Mou Mining failed to cooperate with the Zunhua City Support Zhang-Tang Railway Project Construction Leading Group Office in the coverage compensation work by not providing the filed reserve verification report and development and utilization plan, causing the Leading Group Office to be unable to assess and compensate Mou Mining's relevant losses in accordance with legal procedures. Therefore, the interest losses claimed by Mou Mining for not receiving compensation in a timely manner should not be compensated.

Company B's grounds of appeal: 1. Set aside the first item of the judgment of first instance and amend according to law; 2. All litigation costs to be borne by Guo. Facts and grounds: (1) The judgment of first instance seriously violated legal procedures by rendering a judgment based on evidence that had not been subjected to cross-examination. During the court session on May 17, 2023, the court of first instance failed to organize the parties to conduct cross-examination in this instance on evidentiary materials used as the basis for adjudication, such as the "Calculation Explanation of Mining Right Fee for Mou Mining (Iron Mine)" issued by Company Wu and the "Retrospective Asset Valuation Report on Underground Asset Values Such as Shafts and Tunnels for Company A's Understanding" issued by a certain asset appraisal firm, and instead directly copied the cross-examination opinions of the parties in Case (2018) Hebei Civil First Instance No. 41, rendering the retrial a mere formality. (2) Company B should not be a joint party responsible for the coverage compensation liability. The first instance judgment ordering Company B and Company A to bear joint payment liability lacks legal basis. According to Article 33 of the Mineral Resources Law of the PRC, Article 35 of the Implementing Rules of the Mineral Resources Law of the PRC, and Article 4 of the Original Ministry of Land and Resources Document No. 137, the entity responsible for compensation for coverage of mineral resources by construction projects should be the project developer. In this case, Mou Mining and Company A signed the "Letter of Intent for Compensation for Coverage of Mining Rights by the Proposed Zhang-Tang Railway" in 2009. Company A is the developer of the Zhang-Tang Railway project, while Company B is the construction agent entrusted by Company A to construct the Zhang-Tang Railway project on its behalf. Company B is not the compensation subject in this case and should not bear compensation liability to Guo (Mou Mining). The civil judgment of the Supreme People's Court (2019) Supreme People's Court Final Civil No. 1793 has clearly determined this. (3) Regarding compensation for mining rights. The first instance judgment erroneously compensated Mou Mining by discounting the value of huge resource quantities for which no mining right had been obtained and no mineral resource usage fees had been paid, and applied the law incorrectly. (4) Regarding compensation for underground asset losses such as shafts and tunnels. According to the "Geological Report on Verification of Mineral Resource Reserves of a Certain Iron Mine in Zunhua City, Hebei Province" filed with the Tangshan Bureau of Land and Resources, there were two ore bodies within Mou Mining's mining area: ore body I-4 and ore body II. The filed "Development and Utilization Plan for Mineral Resources of a Certain Iron Mine in Zunhua City, Hebei Province" prepared by Company C did not provide for the development and utilization of ore body II within Mou Mining's mining area. That is, Mou Mining's mining right did not cover ore body II, and it was not entitled to mine ore body II. Its construction of shafts, tunnels, and mining activities within ore body II were all illegal acts, and it has no right to benefit from its illegal conduct. Moreover, Mou Mining has never submitted process documentation for the construction of the shafts and tunnels, making it impossible to prove the actual existence of the shafts and tunnels it claims. (5) Regarding compensation for preliminary expenses, investments, and business suspension losses. In this case, for the preliminary expenses, investments, and business suspension losses of Mou Mining and Mou Dressing Plant, the "Price Assessment Conclusion on Preliminary Expenses, Investments, and Business Suspension Losses of Mou Mining and Mou Dressing Plant" issued by Cangzhou Mou Price Appraisal Office concluded a total of RMB 35,399,115, including blasting-induced damage to residential buildings of RMB 1,103,880. Site inspection revealed no residential buildings within or around the mining area; how could there be blasting-induced damage to residential buildings? If such damage existed, it would have been a cost incurred by Mou Mining during the mining process and should have been amortized into its extraction costs, and therefore should not be compensated. (6) Regarding interest losses. The fundamental reason Mou Mining has not received compensation to date is not that the parties involved in the Zhang-Tang Railway project maliciously delayed or were at fault, but that Mou Mining failed to cooperate with the Zunhua City Support Zhang-Tang Railway Project Construction Leading Group Office in the coverage compensation work by not providing the filed reserve verification report and development and utilization plan in an attempt to seek illegal gains, causing the Leading Group Office to be unable to assess and compensate Mou Mining's relevant losses in accordance with legal procedures. Therefore, the interest losses claimed by Guo for not receiving compensation in a timely manner should not be compensated. (7) The first instance judgment failed to ascertain factual issues highlighted by the Supreme People's Court in its order for retrial (2020) Supreme People's Court Final Civil No. 1281, such as the scope of coverage, the integration of coal mines, and the actual investment in shaft and tunnel projects, before rendering the judgment. The first instance judgment was aware that, in addition to the plaintiff Guo, there was also Wang as the actual operator of Mou Mining, but it did not proactively add Wang or investigate the above unascertained facts; moreover, after Guo voluntarily dissolved the original Mou Mining entity, it did not add Wang, the actual operator, as a necessary joint litigant in accordance with law, which not only left the facts of the case unascertained but also created obstacles to resolving the dispute between Guo and Wang.

Guo's response: (1) The construction project in question constitutes complete coverage of Mou Mining, and all its losses should be compensated. Company A and Company B acknowledge that the construction project's coverage ratio of Mou Mining is 95.04%, which prevents Mou Mining from extending its mining right, and all losses incurred by Mou Mining should be compensated. (2) The total losses that Company A and Company B should compensate Mou Mining amount to RMB 167,179,080 plus related interest. Guo accepts the first instance judgment's determination of losses. A. The Reserve Verification Report by Mou Geological Survey Institute recorded Mou Mining's resource reserves at 1,169,700 tons, based on which the mining right fee loss was calculated at RMB 6,645,200. B. The "Retrospective Asset Valuation Report on Underground Asset Values Such as Shafts and Tunnels for Company A's Understanding" issued by a certain asset appraisal firm (special general partnership) determined that the loss of shaft and tunnel engineering within Mou Mining's mining area was RMB 146,789,700. The main basis for determining the engineering quantities in this assessment report was the "2010 reserve verification report and the current state of shaft and tunnel extraction," meaning the actual completed engineering rather than engineering yet to be constructed, and depreciation had been applied to existing mines using the 2013 development and utilization plan and related supplementary explanations, making the conclusion scientifically sound and reasonable. C. The "Asset Appraisal Report" issued by Company Ji determined that the loss of Mou Mining's machinery, equipment, and building structures totaled RMB 3,044,300, and this portion should be compensated. D. The "Price Assessment Conclusion on Preliminary Expenses, Investments, and Business Suspension Losses of Mou Mining and Mou Dressing Plant" issued by Cangzhou Mou Price Appraisal Office confirmed that the preliminary expenses and investments related to Mou Mining's extraction portion amounted to RMB 10,699,880, and this portion should be compensated. E. From the signing of the "Letter of Intent for Compensation for Coverage of Mining Rights by the Proposed Zhang-Tang Railway" between Mou Mining and Company A in 2009 until the completion and opening of the Zhang-Tang Railway in December 2015, Company B only completed appraisals of mining machinery, equipment, building structures, and preliminary expenses, but did not appraise Mou Mining's mining right loss, shaft and tunnel engineering loss, or other losses. Company B clearly was at fault, and it is fair and reasonable for it to bear corresponding interest losses. (3) Company A and Company B should jointly bear the coverage compensation liability to Mou Mining. Company A, as the investor and developer of the project in question and the owner of the assets, and as the party that signed the "Letter of Intent for Compensation for Coverage of Mining Rights by the Proposed Zhang-Tang Railway," should bear the coverage compensation liability to Mou Mining. Company B has a contractual relationship of entrusted construction with Company A, and its obligations are "to implement the agreements signed by the Ministry of Railways or Party A (Company A) with relevant authorities, to be responsible for coordination and communication with local planning departments, to handle land use approval procedures, and to be responsible for land acquisition and relocation and related work." As the construction agent for the project in question, Company B should bear the coverage compensation liability to Mou Mining together with Company A. (4) Guo, Wang, and other investors have signed an agreement, and all parties agree that the distribution of compensation funds received by Mou Mining will be conducted later. In summary, Guo requests that the court dismiss the appeals of Company A and Company B in accordance with law.

Guo initiated the lawsuit before the court of first instance, requesting: 1. An order that Company A and Company B compensate Guo for mining right losses of RMB 20,622,900, shaft and tunnel engineering value losses of RMB 222,547,769.30, machinery, equipment, and building structure asset losses of RMB 15,038,000, preliminary expenses, investments, and business suspension losses of RMB 35,399,115, totaling RMB 293,607,784; 2. An order that Company A and Company B pay Guo interest on the coverage compensation amounts at the benchmark loan interest rate of the People's Bank of China, provisionally calculated to December 13, 2018 (the date of the application to increase the claim), totaling RMB 43,621,145.35 (calculated from November 13, 2015, until the date of actual payment); 3. Litigation and appraisal costs to be borne by Company A and Company B.

The court of first instance found through trial: On July 28, 2009, Company A, as Party A, and Mou Mining, as Party B, signed the "Letter of Intent for Compensation for Coverage of Mining Rights by the Proposed Zhang-Tang Railway," which mainly provided: "... II. Intentions of Parties A and B: To ensure the implementation of the national key project, the mining right holder and the developer have, through friendly consultation, agreed to the coverage of the mining right. Both parties agree that, after the project is formally established, a compensation agreement shall be negotiated and signed between the parties based on the assessment report on covered mineral resources approved by the provincial department of land and resources, national policies, and relevant regulations."

On October 30, 2010, Company A, as Party A, and Company B, as Party B, signed the "Agreement on Entrusted Construction of the New Zhangjiakou-Tangshan Railway," stipulating that Company A entrusted Company B to carry out all construction management work for the new Zhang-Tang Railway project. On November 12, 2010, with the approval of the former Ministry of Railways, Company B established the Zhangjiakou-Tangshan Engineering Construction Command of Company B to specifically implement the各项工作 under the entrusted construction agreement, including conducting surveys and assessments of mineral resources along the route and carrying out coverage compensation work.

On January 19, 2016, the Zhangjiakou-Tangshan Construction Headquarters of Company B, as Party A (the entrusting party), and the Tangshan Municipal Railway Construction and Management Leading Group Office, as Party B (the受托 party), entered into the "Implementation Agreement on Compensation for Pressured Mineral Resources for the Newly Built Zhangjiakou-Tangshan Railway (Tangshan Section) (II)". The agreement primarily stipulated that Party A is responsible for the disbursement of compensation funds, and Party B is responsible for the specific implementation of the compensation work. The agreement identified a total of five enterprises within the scope of compensation, including a mining operation. The agreement also specified the compensation amounts for each enterprise's mining rights and assets, as determined by relevant appraisal institutions. The compensation amount for the above-ground assets of a certain mining operation was RMB 5,207,974.

On November 8, 2016, the former Zunhua Municipal Bureau of Land and Resources issued the "Explanation on Certain Circumstances of a Mining Operation," which stated: "...Because the construction of the Zhangtang Railway pressured this ore body, to avoid conflict between mining operations and railway construction and operation, the scope of the mining area must be reduced to bypass the Zhangtang Railway. The mining right holder believed that the reserves within the remaining mining area had no mining value and that the mine could no longer operate normally. Therefore, in accordance with relevant policies, the mining right holder did not apply for the renewal and filing procedures for the mining rights in the remaining mining area."

During the trial of this case in the People's Court of Zunhua City, Hebei Province, both parties agreed that the court should entrust an appraisal institution to appraise and evaluate the mining right value and other asset losses claimed by a mining operation. The People's Court of Zunhua City respectively entrusted Company E, a certain price firm of Cangzhou, Company F, and Company X to appraise and evaluate the relevant matters. The above institutions issued the following appraisal and evaluation opinions:

1. On November 30, 2017, Company E issued the "Appraisal Report on the Mining Right of a Mining Operation (Iron Mine)" (Ji Mou Ping [Cai] Zi [2017] No. TO2), concluding that, as of the appraisal base date (November 12, 2011), the assessed value of the mining right of the said mining operation was RMB 20,622,900.

2. On January 5, 2018, Company X issued the "Appraisal Opinion on the Construction Cost of Shafts and Tunnels in the Mining Area of a Mining Operation" (Tang Mou [2018] Jian Zi No. 2), concluding that, based on the existing appraisal data and the entrusted matters, the appraised amount for this project was RMB 222,547,769.30.

3. On November 30, 2017, Company F issued the "Asset Appraisal Verification Report" (Ji Mou Fa Ping Bao Zi [2017] No. 005), concluding that the assessed value of the evaluated assets was RMB 15,038,000 (of which: the assessed value of a mining operation was RMB 3,044,300, and the assessed value of a beneficiation plant was RMB 11,993,700).

4. On November 15, 2017, a certain price firm of Cangzhou issued the "Price Appraisal Conclusion on Preliminary Expenses, Investments, and Business Closure Losses of a Mining Operation and a Beneficiation Plant" (Zi [2017] No. TO42), concluding that the market price of the preliminary expenses, investments, and business closure losses of the mining operation and the beneficiation plant was RMB 35,399,100 (of which: preliminary investment expenses were RMB 19,319,300, and business closure losses were RMB 16,079,800).

The court of first instance organized the parties and the appraisers to cross-examine the above appraisal reports in court. The main disputes between the parties were as follows:

1. Regarding the appraisal report on mining rights. This appraisal report was made based on the market value of the actual resource reserves of 1.1697 million tons. Company A objected to the base date used in the report, the data on resource reserves, and the calculation standard for the compensation amount. After negotiation between the parties, the mining operation agreed to have the appraisal conducted based on the claims of Company B regarding the appraisal base date and the calculation standard for the compensation amount, i.e., using January 21, 2015, as the appraisal base date and the evaluation standard for mining right consideration as determined by the "Hebei Province Administrative Measures for Compensation for Pressured Mineral Resources in Construction Projects" (Ji Guo Tu Zi Fa [2011] No. 41) and the "Hebei Province Administrative Measures for the Payment of Mining Right Consideration" (Ji Zheng Ban [2012] No. 1). Regarding the issue of resource reserves, as the parties could not reach an agreement, Company A claimed that the appraisal should be based on the recorded reserves of 64,100 tons, while the mining operation claimed that it should be based on the actual reserves of 1.1697 million tons. During the in-court cross-examination, both parties agreed that the appraisal institution should issue a conclusion for each of the two reserve data sets. On December 31, 2019, Company E issued the "Calculation Statement for the Mining Right Consideration of a Mining Operation (Iron Mine)" (Ji Mou Ji Zi [2019] No. 01), concluding that, as of the appraisal base date (January 21, 2015), the mining right consideration for the reviewed and filed reserves of 64,100 tons of the mining operation (iron mine) was RMB 276,900, and the mining right consideration for the actual resource reserves of 1.1697 million tons was RMB 6,645,200. Both parties submitted written cross-examination opinions on this evaluation conclusion. Company A claimed that only the mining right consideration of RMB 276,900 corresponding to the filed reserves of 64,100 tons should be compensated, while the mining operation believed that the mining right consideration of RMB 6,645,200 corresponding to the actual resource reserves of 1.1697 million tons should be adopted as the compensation standard. There were no other disputes between the parties.

2. Regarding the appraisal report on shafts and tunnels. With respect to the "Appraisal Opinion on the Construction Cost of Shafts and Tunnels in the Mining Area of a Mining Operation" issued by Company X, Company A believed that, based on the actual extraction of resources in the mining area, some shafts and tunnels had been abandoned due to resource depletion and had no use value, and thus should not be included in the compensation scope. Furthermore, underground works within the scope of compensation should be depreciated based on the useful life corresponding to the allowable extractable resource reserves, rather than compensating for all underground works based on their construction costs. In the first instance trial of this case, both parties agreed to, based on the original appraisal report, the 2010 resource reserve verification report, and the 2013 development and utilization plan, conduct a supplementary appraisal of the compensation amount for underground works in conjunction with the "Eight-Party Registration Table" jointly confirmed by the parties, government departments, and design units. Later, through negotiation, the mining operation agreed that Company A could entrust a certain asset appraisal firm (special general partnership) to re-appraise the compensation amount for underground works. On December 31, 2019, a certain asset appraisal firm (special general partnership) issued a "Retrospective Asset Appraisal Report on the Value of Underground Assets such as Shafts and Tunnels that Company A Intends to Understand." The appraisal conclusion was that the market value of underground assets such as shafts and tunnels within the mining license scope of the mining operation, as of the appraisal base date (January 21, 2015), was RMB 146,789,700. The mining operation submitted a written cross-examination opinion on this appraisal conclusion, recognizing the "three natures" (legality, authenticity, and relevance) of the asset report, but argued that in addition to the shafts and tunnels within the mining license scope, the 16# shaft and tunnel (RMB 5,538,372) near the II ore body were also integrated by it, for which it had invested substantial funds and effort, and that the defendant had confirmed this in the "Eight-Party Registration Table," and thus it should fall within the scope of compensation. Company A argued that because the mining operation had only obtained mining rights for resource reserves of 64,100 tons, according to the appraisal report, the appraised value of the 1#, 2#, and 3# shafts and tunnels corresponding to the 64,100-ton resource reserves was RMB 10,630,976, which should be used as the scope and standard for compensation.

3. Regarding the "Asset Appraisal Verification Report" issued by Company F. Company A argued that the current evidence could not prove that the mining operation was a combined mining and beneficiation enterprise, and thus there was no basis for including the beneficiation plant in the compensation scope. The development and utilization plan of the mining operation mentioned that the project investment was only RMB 1.2 million, but the appraised value of the beneficiation plant was too high. Even if the mining and beneficiation were combined, this beneficiation plant was not exclusively serving the mining operation. The mining operation argued that the beneficiation plant was established specifically for the mining operation, and after the mining operation was pressured, the beneficiation plant could no longer be used, so it should be included in the compensation scope. The new investment of RMB 1.2 million in the development and utilization plan was for the II mining area, and there was a significant discrepancy between the actual extraction situation and the filed situation. The beneficiation capacity and the filed reserves were not proportional. Moreover, every local beneficiation plant was paired with a mining operation, and it was impossible for a mining operation's own beneficiation plant to serve other mining operations.

4. Regarding the "Price Appraisal Conclusion on Preliminary Expenses, Investments, and Business Closure Losses of a Mining Operation and a Beneficiation Plant" issued by a certain price firm of Cangzhou. Company A argued that the preliminary expenses and production suspension losses of the beneficiation plant should not be included in the compensation scope; the mining operation had already ceased production after 2009, so production suspension losses should no longer be supported; moreover, the appraisal of the mining operation's preliminary expenses overlapped with the asset appraisal. The mining operation argued that the preliminary expenses and production suspension losses of the beneficiation plant should be included in the compensation scope, for the same reasons as above. The appraiser from the certain price firm of Cangzhou responded in court that the preliminary investment expenses referred to costs such as road construction, and there was no overlap with other asset appraisals.

Upon examination, the court of first instance found that the mining operation was an individual business, and the actual operator was Guo Mou. After integration, the mining area of the mining operation included the original mining operation operated by Guo Mou, the Guo Moucheng mine operated by Wang Mou, and other unlicensed mines. The Guo Moucheng mine operated by Wang Mou had a mining right certificate before integration, but after integration, that certificate was voided. Within the integrated area, only the mining operation had a mining right certificate, and the other mines did not obtain mining right certificates. On January 8, 2018, Guo Mou and Wang Mou entered into a written agreement regarding the distribution of compensation funds in this case. Later, Wang Mou, dissatisfied with the compensation amount, filed a lawsuit in court requesting the revocation of the agreement. This case is still under trial. Wang Mou did not raise any objection to Guo Mou's assertion of rights in this case, nor did he apply to participate in the litigation as a rights holder. Because the mining operation had not been operating for a long time, on February 28, 2022, the local administrative authority for industry and commerce deregistered the mining operation. The actual area of the mining operation's mining area that was pressured was 95.04%, and the parties had no dispute over the scope of the pressure. The verified resource reserves within the original mining certificate boundary of the former iron mine were 47,700 tons, and the verified resource reserves outside the boundary were 16,400 tons, totaling 64,100 tons. This filed reserve was not within the pressured area. The 1.1 million tons of mineral reserves within the pressured area were not filed. In 2010, the mining operation conducted a detailed survey of the reserves within the integrated area. The additional 1.1 million tons were mainly in the II ore body (i.e., the Guo Moucheng mine). The II ore body was within the integrated area and fell within the pressured area. The mining operation claimed that because the Zhangtang Railway pressed this ore body, it was impossible to complete the renewal and filing procedures for the mining rights in the remaining mining area. Additionally, there were substantial underground works and above-ground assets within the pressured area. Company A and Company B claimed that the mining operation had already ceased extraction before the construction of the railway, but they did not provide sufficient reliable evidence to prove this.

The court of first instance further found: The beneficiation plant was a sole proprietorship enterprise established by Guo Mou in 2005. The beneficiation plant was located in Luowenyu Village, southeast of Zunhua city center, approximately 30 kilometers away from the mining operation, and was not within the integrated area of the mining operation; it was an independent entity. The losses of the beneficiation plant's mechanical equipment, buildings and structures, and tailings pond were appraised at RMB 11,993,700, losses for land acquisition and tree acquisition were RMB 7,486,100, and preliminary investment losses were RMB 1,133,285, totaling RMB 20,613,085.

The court of first instance held that the core issues in dispute between the parties in this case were: 1. Whether Guo Mou was the proper plaintiff; 2. How to determine the cause of action in this case; 3. How to determine the scope, standard, and amount of compensation payable by Company A to the mining operation for the pressure; 4. Whether interest on the compensation amount should be supported; 5. Whether Company B was a proper defendant in this case.

(1) Regarding whether Guo Mou was the proper plaintiff. The original plaintiff in this case was the mining operation. The mining operation was integrated from the original mining operation operated by Guo Mou, the Guo Moucheng mine operated by Wang Mou, and other mines. After integration, only one mining right certificate existed within the integrated area, which was for the mining operation. As the holder of the mining right, the mining operation was entitled to claim compensation for the loss of mineral resources due to pressure. During the litigation, the mining operation underwent deregistration procedures, and this entity no longer exists and cannot continue to exercise litigation rights. Therefore, the operator of the mining operation, Guo Mou, should be the litigation subject, and the plaintiff in this case should be changed to Guo Mou. The rights and interests of other mineral operators within the integrated area of the mining operation are matters of rights and obligations between them and Guo Mou, which can be resolved separately and do not need to be added to this litigation. Furthermore, during the litigation of this case, Wang Mou never objected to the plaintiff status of the mining operation or Guo Mou, nor did he apply to this court to join the litigation as a rights holder. Therefore, the arguments of Company A and Company B that Guo Mou was not a proper plaintiff lacked basis, and this court did not support them.

(2) Regarding the cause of action in this case. According to the provisions of the Civil Code of the People's Republic of China, mining rights fall within the scope of usufructuary rights. The infringement by the project construction party on the rights of the holder of the pressured mining right is essentially an impact on the possession, use, and profit rights enjoyed by the holder based on the usufructuary right, i.e., it is closely related to the possession and attribution of the usufructuary right. It is most appropriate to handle it under the category of property rights protection disputes. Property damage disputes themselves are a type of cause of action under the category of property rights protection disputes. Since Company A went through the approval procedures for the construction of the Zhangtang Railway, which is a lawful act, it is more appropriate to designate the cause of action in this case as a dispute over compensation for property damage.

(3) Regarding the scope, standard, and amount of compensation for the mining operation. Company A's investment in constructing the Zhangtang Railway resulted in the mining operation being pressured and unable to continue extraction and operation. The parties have no objection that Company A should compensate for the various losses caused to the mining operation in accordance with the law. Regarding the scope, standard, and amount of compensation for the mining operation, during the proceedings of this case, relevant appraisal institutions were entrusted to appraise and evaluate the four categories of losses claimed by the mining operation. After this court organized the parties to cross-examine the appraisal conclusions and the appraisers provided explanations, although the parties still had multiple disputes over the appraisal conclusions, each appraisal institution had the legal qualifications, the procedures were lawful, and the appraisal opinions they issued could serve as a reference basis for this court to determine the compensation for the mining operation. Company A and Company B argued that the appraisal reports were not lawful and that a new appraisal should be conducted, but the basis was insufficient, and this court did not adopt that argument.

1. Compensation for the value of mining rights. Regarding this compensation, the parties reached an agreement on the appraisal base date and the calculation standard for the compensation amount, i.e., using January 21, 2015, as the base date and calculating the compensation amount based on the standard for the payment of mining right consideration by government departments on that base date. As for the scope of compensation, although Company A claimed that only the mining right consideration for the filed resource reserves of 64,100 tons should be compensated, first of all, the impact of the construction of the Zhangtang Railway on the mining operation was not merely that the filed 64,100 tons of resources could not be extracted, nor was it merely that the resources within 1,000 meters on both sides of the railway could not be extracted. Instead, it resulted in the complete closure of the mining operation, making all 1.1697 million tons of proven resources unextractable. Secondly, according to the "Explanation on Certain Circumstances of a Mining Operation" issued by the former Zunhua Municipal Bureau of Land and Resources on November 8, 2016, the reason the mining operation did not apply for the renewal and filing procedures for the mining rights in the remaining mining area was precisely because the pressure from the Zhangtang Railway construction made it impossible for the mine to operate normally, and the resource reserves in the remaining mining area lost their extraction value. Although Company A and Company B did not accept this explanation, claiming that the railway construction did not render the entire mining operation unextractable, they also did not provide other sufficient and effective evidence to prove this. Now that the mining operation no longer exists and the objective situation at that time cannot be restored, neither party has further adduced evidence on this point. It can only be determined through the existing evidence that the construction of the Zhangtang Railway caused the entire mining operation to be unextractable. The mining operation's failure to apply for the filing of this portion of resources was not due to its own fault. Company A's argument that compensation should not be provided because this portion of resources was not filed cannot be sustained. Third, the parties agreed to use the standard for the payment of mining right consideration by government departments as the compensation standard. This is a jointly determined reference standard for calculating the amount of compensation. It is unrelated to whether the mining right consideration for this portion of resources was actually paid to the government department. Moreover, judging from the appraisal conclusions of the mining right value before and after the litigation by the appraisal institution, the market expectation benefit that the mining operation had for the pressured mineral resources should be far greater than the mining right consideration it should have paid. Therefore, the parties' agreement to use the mining right consideration that should be paid as the compensation amount does not violate the principle of fairness. Company A's argument that compensation should not be provided because this portion of resources was not filed also cannot be sustained. In summary, this court determines that the compensation amount for the value of the mining right of the mining operation is RMB 6,645,200.

2. Compensation for shafts and tunnels. During the proceedings of this case, after Company X issued the "Appraisal Opinion on the Construction Cost of Shafts and Tunnels in the Mining Area of a Mining Operation" (appraisal conclusion of RMB 222,547,769.30), Company A objected to the evaluation of the value of shaft and tunnel works based on construction costs and the scope of shaft and tunnel works. Later, through negotiation, the mining operation agreed that Company A could entrust a certain asset appraisal firm (special general partnership) to conduct a new appraisal in accordance with Company A's proposal to deduct the abandoned shafts and tunnels (4#, 7#, J19#) and to depreciate based on the useful life. The appraisal conclusion was RMB 146,789,700. Although Company A argued that the mining operation only had filed resource reserves of 64,100 tons, and thus only the appraised value of the 1#, 2#, and 3# shaft and tunnel works within this scope, RMB 10,630,976, should be compensated, based on the same reasoning for determining the scope of compensation for the mining right value, this court determines that Company A should compensate for all shaft and tunnel works within the mining license scope of the mining operation (excluding the abandoned 4#, 7#, and J19# shaft and tunnel works), and the compensation amount is RMB 146,789,700. In addition, the mining operation claimed that the 16# shaft and tunnel near the II ore body were integrated by it and should also be compensated. In this regard, given that this shaft and tunnel works are located outside the mining license scope of the mining operation and were not reflected in the 2010 resource reserve verification report or the 2013 development and utilization plan, even if the 16# shaft and tunnel were recorded in the "Eight-Party Registration Table," this does not necessarily mean that they would ultimately be included in the compensation scope. Therefore, the mining operation's claim for compensation of RMB 5,538,372 for the 16# shaft and tunnel is not supported. Company A and Company B argued that during the on-site inspection, the parties did not actually go down into the mine for inspection, and the data in the Eight-Party Registration Table was not truthful. However, when the site was inspected, Company A and Company B were both present and did not request to go down into the mine for inspection. The conditions for a new inspection no longer exist. Therefore, this court does not support the arguments of Company A and Company B.

3. Regarding the value of compensation for assets. The appraisal value of this portion of assets, as assessed by the appraisal institution based on the property inventory jointly inventoried by multiple parties, was RMB 15,038,000, of which the appraised value of assets within a certain mining area was RMB 3,044,300, and the appraised value of assets of a certain mineral processing plant was RMB 11,993,700. Party A should compensate for the loss of assets of the certain mining area amounting to RMB 3,044,300. However, the certain mineral processing plant is a sole proprietorship enterprise registered with the industry and commerce authorities, which is an independent entity and is not located within the certain mining area, nor does it fall within the scope of the area affected by the overlying. Although the certain mining company claimed that Guo had established the certain mineral processing plant solely to serve the certain mining company, the certain mineral processing plant is 30 kilometers away from the certain mining area. The certain mining company did not provide evidence to prove that after the certain mining company ceased operations, the certain mineral processing plant was also unable to produce or operate. Therefore, it cannot be determined that the appraisal loss of assets of the certain mineral processing plant was caused by the railway overlying. The certain mineral processing plant should not be included in the scope of compensation. In summary, Party A should not compensate for the assets of the certain mineral processing plant with an appraised value of RMB 11,993,700.

4. Regarding compensation for preliminary investments and losses due to business suspension. The appraisal institution's assessment of the preliminary investments and business suspension losses of the certain mining company and the certain mineral processing plant amounted to RMB 35,399,100, of which the preliminary investment costs of the certain mineral processing plant were RMB 1,133,285, and the losses from land acquisition and tree acquisition were RMB 7,486,100. According to the detailed list in the appraisal institution's evaluation report, the preliminary investment costs of the certain mining company mainly included expenses for road construction, land leveling, land acquisition, tree acquisition, and blasting vibration compensation. These items did not overlap with other compensation items such as assets and facilities. Party A should compensate for the preliminary investment costs of the certain mining company. Regarding the preliminary investment costs and losses from land acquisition and tree acquisition of the certain mineral processing plant, for the same reasons as the aforementioned compensation for assets, the certain mining company also could not prove that these losses were related to the railway overlying. Therefore, Party A shall not compensate for the preliminary investment costs of the certain mineral processing plant of RMB 1,133,285 and the losses from land acquisition and tree acquisition of RMB 7,486,100. Regarding the business suspension losses of RMB 16,079,800, according to the appraisal institution's evaluation report, it can be seen that this loss amount was calculated based on the monthly average output value and profit of the certain mining company before its suspension, covering the profits from 2010 to 2017. Given that the compensation for the value of mining rights had already included compensation for 1.1697 million tons of resource price based on government charging standards, this compensation overlapped with the aforementioned business suspension losses. Therefore, the court no longer supported the business suspension losses of RMB 16,079,800.

(4) Regarding the issue of interest on various compensation amounts. Considering that since the signing of the "Letter of Intent for Compensation for Overlying Mining Rights of the Proposed Zhangjiakou-Tangshan Railway" between Party A and the certain mining company in 2009, more than ten years have elapsed. Due to the parties' failure to reach an agreement on the amount of compensation, the certain mining company has not actually received the compensation payable for a long time, resulting in objective losses of capital interest. Considering the principle of fairness, Party A should reasonably share this. The court, in its discretion, determined that Party A shall pay interest on the compensation payable from the date of filing this lawsuit, i.e., January 17, 2017, at the loan interest rate of the same period and same category of the People's Bank of China (or the loan prime rate of the same period published by the National Interbank Funding Center).

(5) Regarding the subject qualification and responsibility of Party B. Because Party B was entrusted by Party A to act as the agent for the construction management of the entire Zhangjiakou-Tangshan Railway project, including investigation, assessment, and overlying compensation work for mineral resources along the line. At the same time, the Zhangjiakou-Tangshan Railway Engineering Construction Headquarters (Party A) established by Party B and the Tangshan Railway Construction and Management Leading Group Office (Party B) signed the "Implementation Agreement on Compensation for Overlying Minerals for the New Zhangjiakou-Tangshan Railway (Tangshan Section) (Part 2)". The agreement stipulated that Party A was responsible for the disbursement of compensation and identified a list of five mining enterprises entitled to compensation, including the certain mining company. Party B, being responsible for both the construction management of the Zhangjiakou-Tangshan Railway project and the disbursement of compensation to the overlying enterprises, qualified as a defendant in this case and should bear the overlying compensation liability jointly with Party A.

In summary, the total compensation payable by Party A and Party B to the certain mining company for various items shall be: RMB 6,645,200 + RMB 146,789,700 + RMB 15,038,000 + RMB 19,319,300 - RMB 20,613,085 = RMB 167,179,115. The court of first instance, in accordance with Articles 327 and 329 of the Civil Code of the People's Republic of China, ruled as follows: 1. Party A and Party B shall jointly pay Guo compensation of RMB 167,179,115 and interest within 30 days from the effective date of the judgment. Interest shall be calculated at the loan interest rate of the same period and same category of the People's Bank of China from January 17, 2017, to August 19, 2019, and from August 20, 2019, to the date of actual payment at the loan prime rate of the same period published by the National Interbank Funding Center; 2. Guo's other claims were dismissed. The acceptance fee for the first instance was RMB 1,509,839, with Guo bearing RMB 541,800 and Party B and Party A jointly bearing RMB 968,039.

This court requested Party A to submit the approval of the project proposal by the National Development and Reform Commission as recorded in Document No. 2009/1905 (Fa Gai Ji Chu [2009] No. 1905) referred to in the "Reply on the Overlying of Mineral Resources for the 'New Zhangjiakou-Tangshan Railway Construction Project'" (Ji Guo Tu Zi Ya Pi Zi [2009] No. 05) issued by the former Hebei Provincial Department of Land and Resources to Party A, as well as the "Investigation and Assessment Report on Overlying Mineral Resources for the New Zhangjiakou-Tangshan Railway Construction Project" prepared by the Shijiazhuang Comprehensive Geological Brigade of the Hebei Provincial Bureau of Geology and Mineral Resources, among other evidentiary materials.
