This court holds that paragraph 2 of Article 1 of the "Several Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on the Temporal Effect of the Application of the Civil Code of the People's Republic of China" states: "For civil dispute cases arising from legal facts before the implementation of the Civil Code, the provisions of the laws and judicial interpretations in force at that time shall apply, unless otherwise provided by laws and judicial interpretations." Given that the facts of this case occurred before the implementation of the Civil Code of the People's Republic of China and there are no exceptions, the laws and judicial interpretations in force at that time shall apply to this case. The first-instance judgment, without explanation, directly applied the provisions of the Civil Code, which was erroneous and should be corrected.

Based on the parties' submissions and the specific facts of this case, the issues in dispute in this second instance are as follows: (1) whether the pressure in this case constitutes full pressure or partial pressure; if partial, how the scope of pressure should be determined; (2) how the scope, standard, amount, and interest of the pressure compensation should be determined; (3) whether Company B should bear joint liability with Company A for the payment of the pressure compensation. These issues are addressed below.

(1) Regarding whether the pressure in this case constitutes full pressure or partial pressure; if partial, how the scope of pressure should be determined.

Pressure on mineral resources refers to a situation where a construction project physically or spatially overlaps with an exploration area or a mining area, or, even if not overlapping, according to relevant regulations, exploration or mining activities are prohibited or restricted within a certain range around or above and below the construction project, resulting in the total or partial inability to exploit and utilize mineral resources within the exploration area or mining area, and the inability to exercise the mining rights normally. In judicial practice, even if the construction project does not cause full pressure, if it objectively leads to the total inability to exploit and utilize mineral resources within the exploration area or mining area, it shall also be deemed as full pressure. In this case, based on the "Survey and Assessment Report on Mineral Resources Pressured by the Construction Land of the New Zhangjiakou-Tangshan Railway Project" approved by the former Hebei Provincial Department of Land and Resources on September 23, 2009, Mou Mining was not within the pressured area. However, on January 21, 2015, the General Office of the Hebei Provincial People's Government issued the "Notice on the Work of Assessing and Compensating for Pressure on Mines by the Zhangtang Railway," which adjusted the scope of assessment and compensation for pressure on mines by the Zhangtang Railway to within 1,000 meters on both sides of the railway. This resulted in 95.04% of the mining area of Mou Mining being pressured by the Zhangtang Railway, making it impossible to continue exploiting and utilizing the mineral resources within the mining area and preventing the normal exercise of the mining rights of Mou Mining. During the second instance proceedings, the parties had no dispute over the above scope of pressure. Both Company A and Company B acknowledged that the pressure in this case constitutes full pressure, and this court confirms that.

(2) Regarding how the scope, standard, amount, and interest of the pressure compensation in this case should be determined.

1. Regarding the issue of compensation or damages.

Article 123 of the former Property Law of the PRC provides: "The rights to exploration, mining, water use, and to engage in aquaculture and fishing using waters and tidal flats, lawfully obtained, are protected by law." Based on the facts found in this case, the Mou Mining transferred to Guo obtained a mining license in 2005, valid until September 2010; after the integration of the mining area, a new mining license was issued in 2009, valid until May 4, 2011; later, due to the pressure from the Zhangtang Railway, the mining right of Mou Mining was not renewed. The lawfully obtained mining right of Mou Mining shall be protected by law. According to Article 6 of the former Tort Liability Law of the PRC, which stipulates that "a person who through his fault infringes upon the civil rights and interests of another shall bear tort liability," for Mou Mining to claim that Company A and Company B committed tort, it must prove that Company A and Company B were at fault in the act of pressuring mineral resources. Given that the Zhangtang Railway is a major national construction project approved by the National Development and Reform Commission and has a public welfare nature; Company A, as the construction entity, lawfully commissioned a third party to conduct a survey and assessment of the pressure on mineral resources along the railway and obtained pressure approval from the competent department of natural resources; Company B, as the construction agent, was entrusted to carry out the construction lawfully. Company A and Company B had no fault in the pressure act in this case and shall not bear liability for tort damages. Guo's claim for compensation for losses from Company A and Company B cannot be sustained. However, because the pressure from the Zhangtang Railway project caused Mou Mining (Guo) to be unable to continue exercising its mining rights, resulting in damage to its lawful interests, it is entitled to corresponding compensation according to law.

Regarding compensation for pressure on mineral resources, the Mineral Resources Law of the PRC and related administrative regulations and judicial interpretations have no specific provisions on pressure compensation and the scope of compensation. Article 4, paragraph 3 of Document No. 137 of the former Ministry of Land and Resources provides: "If a construction project pressures mineral resources for which mining rights have already been established, the new land user shall also simultaneously enter into an agreement with the mining right holder. The agreement shall include the mining right holder's consent to waive the pressured mining area and related compensation content. The scope of compensation shall in principle include: 1. the amount payable for the reserves of resources pressured by the mining right holder under current market conditions (excluding those obtained gratuitously); 2. direct losses such as the exploration investment shared by the pressured mineral resources, investment in already constructed mining facilities, and costs of relocating corresponding facilities." This normative document establishes the loss items that the scope of compensation for mining rights pressure should in principle include. Although it does not exclude other possible losses, it implies a general principle of compensating for direct losses. This court, in Civil Judgment (2019) No. 1793 of the Supreme People's Court, clarified: "Considering that railway and related construction projects often involve national security and development interests, the resulting pressure on mining rights can, in a sense, be deemed as being for the public interest. In the absence of clear legal or administrative regulations on the standard and scope of compensation for lawful pressure on mining rights, and with reference to the spirit of Document No. 137, in principle, compensating for direct losses caused to the mining rights holder is consistent with the current basic national conditions of our country. The specific compensation loss items may be determined comprehensively by considering the specific circumstances of each case." Given that both this case and the case in Civil Judgment (2019) No. 1793 of the Supreme People's Court involve pressure compensation for the Zhangtang Railway, they may be handled by analogy.

2. Regarding the specific scope, standard, and amount of compensation in this case.

Company A, due to its investment in constructing the Zhangtang Railway, caused Mou Mining to be pressured and unable to continue mining operations. It shall compensate for all direct losses thus caused according to law. Both parties have no objection to this. The specific scope of compensation claimed by Guo in this case includes: loss of mining right value of RMB 20,622,900; loss of shaft and tunnel project value of RMB 222,547,769.30; loss of mechanical equipment, buildings, and structures valued at RMB 15,038,000; and prior expenses, investments, and business suspension losses of RMB 35,399,115, totaling RMB 293,607,784. The first-instance judgment supported compensation for mining right value of RMB 6,645,200; compensation for shafts and tunnels of RMB 146,789,700; compensation for surface assets of RMB 3,044,300; and compensation for prior investment expenses of RMB 10,699,915, totaling RMB 167,179,115. The first-instance judgment handled the compensation in this case with reference to the provisions of Document No. 137 of the former Ministry of Land and Resources and in accordance with the general principle of compensating for direct losses from pressure. Company A had no objection to this, except for disputes over the specific scope, standard, and amount of compensation (except for the compensation of RMB 3,044,300 for above-ground assets such as machinery, equipment, and buildings of Mou Mining). Based on the undisputed basic facts confirmed by the parties and the evidence materials on file, the compensation for the disputed items of mining right value loss, shaft and tunnel loss, and prior investment expenses are analyzed as follows:

(1) Loss of mining right value.

During the retrial process after the case was remanded, both parties reached an agreement on the valuation base date and the calculation standard for compensation for the mining right value of Mou Mining. They agreed to take January 21, 2015, as the valuation base date and to calculate compensation based on the standard for mining rights fees that the government department should collect on that base date. This consensus between the parties is generally consistent with the spirit of Document No. 137 of the former Ministry of Land and Resources. The dispute between the parties is whether the compensation for mining right value should be calculated based on the verified and recorded mineral resource reserves of 64,100 tons approved by the competent department of natural resources (评审备案) or on the 1,169,700 tons (including the verified and recorded 64,100 tons) of mineral resource reserves that Mou Mining self-commissioned for exploration and verification, thereby determining the compensation amount for mining right value.

The verification and recording of mineral resource reserves (矿产资源储量评审备案) refers to an administrative act whereby the competent department of natural resources, in fulfillment of the legal requirements of state ownership of mineral resources and the owner's responsibilities, examines and confirms the mineral resource reserves declared by an applicant upon application, enters them into the national mineral resource physical account, and uses them as an important basis for state management of mineral resources. On February 14, 2014, the former Ministry of Land and Resources published the retained list of 45 administrative approval items, among which "verification, recording, and registration approval of mineral resource reserves" was still one of them (item number 12034). Article 13 of the Mineral Resources Law of the PRC provides: "The mineral reserve approval authority of the State Council or the mineral reserve approval authority of a province, autonomous region, or municipality directly under the Central Government is responsible for examining and approving exploration reports for use in mine construction design, and shall reply to the reporting entity within the prescribed time limit. Exploration reports that have not been approved shall not be used as the basis for mine construction design." Article 4 of the former "Measures for the Verification and Recognition of Mineral Resource Reserves" (Guo Tu Zi Fa [1999] No. 205) promulgated by the former Ministry of Land and Resources, the former State Development Planning Commission, the former State Economic and Trade Commission, the People's Bank of China, and the China Securities Regulatory Commission provides: "The state implements unified management of the verification and recognition of mineral resource reserves." Article 5 provides: "The following mineral resource reserves must be verified and recognized in accordance with these Measures: (1) mineral resource reserves applied for as the basis for mining rights or water extraction permits for use in mine construction design; ... (5) mineral resource reserves that have undergone significant changes within a mining area and require re-verification and recognition; (6) other circumstances of mineral resource reserves that the Ministry of Land and Resources deems should be verified and recognized." In 2003, Article 1 of the former "Notice on Strengthening the Supervision and Management of Verification of Mineral Resource Reserves" (Guo Tu Zi Fa [2003] No. 136) promulgated by the former Ministry of Land and Resources provided: "From the date of issuance of this notice, the administrative department of land and resources will no longer recognize mineral resource reserves but will establish a filing management system." The "Notice of the General Office of the Ministry of Natural Resources on Several Matters Concerning the Filing of Verification of Mineral Resource Reserves" (Zi Ran Zi Ban Fa [2020] No. 26) effective from May 19, 2020, and the "Opinions of the Ministry of Natural Resources on Several Matters Concerning Deepening the Reform of Mineral Resource Management" (Zi Ran Zi Gui [2023] No. 6) effective from July 26, 2023, both clarify that for oil and gas minerals, if the proven geological reserves change during the exploration and mining period, and for other minerals, if the resource volume changes significantly during the mining period (change exceeding 30% or reaching medium-scale or above), and for construction projects that pressure important minerals, a mineral resource reserve report complying with relevant standards and specifications shall be prepared and submitted for verification and filing. Thus, the system of verification and filing of mineral resource reserves has continued to the present. If a mining right holder fails to apply for verification and filing of mineral resource reserves according to law, the authenticity of the corresponding mineral resource reserves cannot be confirmed, which will lead to adverse legal consequences, and the civil rights and interests claimed on that basis may be difficult to support.

In this case, in March 2010, a Mou Geological Survey Institute, commissioned by Mou Mining, issued a reserve verification report. On April 27, 2013, the Mou Geological Survey Institute engaged three experts to review the above verification report and issued an expert panel review opinion for the "Reserve Verification Report" of the Mou Geological Survey Institute. However, the above reserve verification report was not submitted to the competent department of natural resources for verification and recording according to law, and the review opinion letter was not issued after the review by experts organized by the competent department of natural resources. Guo did not give a reasonable explanation as to why it was not submitted for verification and recording. Moreover, during the mining area integration in 2006, the Second Geological Brigade of the Hebei Province Geological Exploration Bureau, commissioned by the former Zunhua City Bureau of Land and Resources and the mining enterprise, conducted verification of resource reserves in the integrated area of Mou Mining, then submitted the "Geological Report on Verification of Resource Reserves of an Iron Mine in Zunhua City, Hebei Province," which was reviewed and recorded by the former Hebei Provincial Department of Land and Resources. Based on this, the former Hebei Provincial Department of Land and Resources issued a new mining license to Mou Mining, and Mou Mining did not raise any objection. For a comprehensive review and assessment of the pressure on mining rights from the Zhangtang Railway, in July 2009, the Shijiazhuang Comprehensive Geological Brigade of the Hebei Province Bureau of Geology and Mineral Resources completed the "Survey and Assessment Report on Mineral Resources Pressured by the Construction Land of the New Zhangjiakou-Tangshan Railway Project" and submitted it for review by the Reserve Review Center of the former Hebei Provincial Department of Land and Resources. Neither the above verification of mineral resource reserves nor the survey and assessment work discovered that the II ore body contained resource reserves that had not yet been explored. The Mou Geological Survey Institute, commissioned by Mou Mining on March 1, 2010, and based solely on "mainly compiling and studying past geological data, field work, and indoor report writing," issued a reserve verification report within the same month (without a specific date), discovering that the II ore body still contained huge resource reserves (1,105,600 tons) that had not been previously discovered, which also goes against common sense. Given that the "Reserve Verification Report" of the Mou Geological Survey Institute was not submitted to the competent department of natural resources for verification and recording according to law, during the several years from the time Mou Mining (Guo) obtained the "Reserve Verification Report" of the Mou Geological Survey Institute until the occurrence of this dispute, there is also no evidence that Mou Mining (Guo) applied for verification and recording from the local competent department of natural resources. Without lawfully conducting verification and recording by the competent department of natural resources, the authenticity of the "Reserve Verification Report" of the Mou Geological Survey Institute is difficult to confirm, and the authenticity of the mineral resource reserves stated therein is also difficult to confirm.

In summary, according to the evaluation conclusion of the "Calculation Explanation of Mining Right Fees for Mou Mining (Iron Mine)" issued by Company E, commissioned by the court, the mining right fees of RMB 276,900 corresponding to the mineral resource reserves of 64,100 tons verified and recorded by the competent department of natural resources should be taken as the loss of mining right value in this case, to be compensated by Company A according to law. The first-instance judgment, based on the resource reserves of 1,169,700 tons stated in the "Reserve Verification Report" of the Mou Geological Survey Institute (which was not verified and recorded by the competent department of natural resources), erred in determining the compensation for the loss of mining right value at RMB 6,645,200, and this should be corrected.

(2) Loss of shaft and tunnel project value.

By reference to the provisions of Document No. 137 of the former Ministry of Land and Resources, the scope of pressure compensation also includes losses from "exploration investment shared by the pressured mineral resources and investment in already constructed mining facilities." The shafts and tunnels claimed by Guo can be classified as such direct losses. During the integration of Mou Mining in 2006, the "Geological Report on Verification of Resource Reserves of an Iron Mine in Zunhua City, Hebei Province" issued by the Second Geological Brigade of the Hebei Province Geological Exploration Bureau and the review opinion letter issued by the former Tangshan City Bureau of Land and Resources stated that within the integrated area there were a dozen shafts, but only shafts 1#, 2#, and 3# were in production. The integrated Mou Mining mining area included the I-4 ore body and the II ore body (i.e., Guo's urban ore body). The I-4 ore body had proven 122b economic basic reserves of 64,100 tons; the II ore body had proven reserves of 17,800 tons, with the shaft mouths and initial mining area within the mining area, but the proven reserves were already distributed outside the integrated area. In August 2007, the "Development and Utilization Plan for Mineral Resources of an Iron Mine in Zunhua City, Hebei Province" issued by Company C (which underwent verification and recording) stated: "The proven reserves of the I-4 ore body are all distributed within the mining area. After this verification, the proven 122b economic basic reserves within the mining area are 64,100 tons." "Currently, the remaining resource reserves of the II ore body exceed the integrated area scope, i.e., the proven reserves are already distributed outside the integrated area." "Within the integrated area, there are currently a dozen shafts, but only shafts 1#, 2#, and 3# are in production. The mine uses vertical shaft development, with the main mining level currently at -3m to -6m. Since the remaining resource reserves of the II ore body exceed the mining area scope, i.e., the proven reserves are already distributed outside the mining area, this design only considers the design of the I-4 ore body." Therefore, given that the authenticity of the "Reserve Verification Report" of the Mou Geological Survey Institute cannot be confirmed, the newly added resource reserves of the II ore body, which were self-commissioned for verification by Mou Mining and not verified and recorded by the competent department of natural resources, are difficult to determine. Moreover, the remaining resource reserves of the II ore body have exceeded the scope of the mining area (integrated area), and Mou Mining has no substantive rights over them. Therefore, Mou Mining (Guo)'s request for Company A to compensate for the shaft and tunnel projects corresponding to the II ore body lacks sufficient reasoning. As for the shafts and tunnels related to the RFe ore body, section 5.7 of the "Reserve Verification Report" of the Mou Geological Survey Institute clearly states: "In this calculation of resource reserves, there are four RFe ore bodies (approximately 600,000 tons) with TFe less than 25%, so this verification did not estimate them." Moreover, the integration of Mou Mining in 2006 did not involve or include the RFe ore body, so the shafts and tunnels related to the RFe ore body should also not fall within the scope of pressure compensation in this case. In addition, Mou Mining (Guo) also did not submit evidence to prove that it actually invested in constructing the shaft and tunnel projects related to the II ore body and the RFe ore body, nor the specific time of investment and construction, the amount invested, or the construction and acceptance drawings. In summary, there is factual basis for not compensating for the losses of shafts and tunnels related to the II ore body and the RFe ore body in this case, and this is also consistent with the actual circumstances of this case.

Regarding the I-4 ore body, it has mineral resource reserves of 64,100 tons that have been verified and recorded by the competent department of natural resources. According to the "Development and Utilization Plan for Mineral Resources of Mou Mining" issued by Company D in May 2013, and the "Retrospective Asset Evaluation Report on the Value of Shaft and Tunnel Underground Assets of Company A" issued by a certain Asset Appraisal Firm (special general partnership) in 2019, the development system of the I-4 ore body includes five shafts and tunnels: shafts 1#, 2#, 3#, 4#, and 7#. Shafts 4# and 7# are located within the rock movement boundary, posing safety hazards, and are both abandoned. The design utilizes the original shaft 1# as the main shaft... the design utilizes the original shaft 2# as the auxiliary shaft... the design utilizes the original shaft 3# as the south return air shaft... the design utilizes the original shaft 5# as the north return air shaft... air enters from the auxiliary shaft, and the south and north form a complete ventilation system. Thus, shafts 1#, 2#, and 3# are still usable, while shaft 5# was originally used for mining the RFe ore body resources but is designed to be used as a ventilation shaft for mining the I-4 ore body resources, and can be considered as part of the shaft and tunnel projects for the I-4 ore body to be compensated. Based on the "Detailed Schedule of Inventory and Appraisal of Fixed Assets - Shaft and Tunnel Facilities" attached to the "Retrospective Asset Evaluation Report on the Value of Shaft and Tunnel Underground Assets of Company A," the total appraised value of the shaft and tunnel projects for shafts 1#, 2#, and 3# is RMB 10,630,976, and the appraised value of the shaft and tunnel project for shaft 5# is RMB 13,794,676. Therefore, the total value of shaft and tunnel projects related to the I-4 ore body is RMB 24,425,652 (RMB 10,630,976 + RMB 13,794,676), to be compensated by Company A.

(3) Prior investment expenses.

On November 15, 2017, upon the entrustment of the Zunhua City People's Court, a certain price appraisal firm in Cangzhou issued the "Price Appraisal Conclusion on Preliminary Expenses, Investments, and Business Cessation Losses of a Certain Mining Operation and a Certain Dressing Plant," in which the preliminary investment expenses of RMB 18,185,980 included: (1) nine items such as safety impact assessment fees, water and soil conservation facility compensation, mineral resource mining registration fees, and mining right usage fees, totaling RMB 1,043,100; (2) 16 payments compensating for residential building losses caused by blasting vibrations, totaling RMB 1,103,880; (3) wages for watchmen of the certain mining operation (2010-2016), totaling RMB 579,600; (4) 17 payments for land and tree compensation for the certain mining operation, totaling RMB 6,503,200; (5) 7 payments for tree compensation for the certain mining operation, totaling RMB 1,470,100; and (6) 30 payments for land and tree compensation for the Luowenyu Village dressing plant, totaling RMB 7,486,100. The first-instance judgment supported items (1) through (5) of the preliminary expenses, totaling RMB 10,699,880. Company A appealed, arguing that only items (1) and (3) should be supported, totaling RMB 1,622,700 (RMB 1,043,100 + RMB 579,600). This Court holds that item (2) of the above preliminary investment expenses, "16 payments compensating for residential building losses caused by blasting vibrations of RMB 1,103,880," arose from losses to surrounding residential buildings caused by blasting vibrations from Mining A before it was overlain, and has no causal relationship with Company A's overlaying act. Company A's claim that this portion of losses should not be compensated has corresponding grounds and should be supported. Items (4), the 17 payments for land and tree compensation for Mining A totaling RMB 6,503,200, and (5), the 7 payments for tree compensation totaling RMB 1,470,100, were necessary expenses paid for subsequent mining and could have been offset in subsequent mining operations. However, because Company A's subsequent overlaying rendered mining impossible, compensating this portion of losses by Company A is reasonable. Item (6), the 30 payments for land and tree compensation for the Luowenyu Village dressing plant, was not supported in the first-instance judgment, and Guo did not appeal, which this Court confirms. The above four preliminary expenses total RMB 9,596,000 (RMB 1,622,700 + RMB 6,503,200 + RMB 1,470,100). Company A argued that the appraised amounts of the above land and tree compensation were excessively high, but did not provide sufficient evidence to support this claim, so it is not upheld.

In summary, including the loss of machinery, equipment, and buildings of RMB 3,044,300 to which Company A had no objection, Company A shall, in accordance with law, compensate Mining A (Guo) for various losses totaling RMB 37,342,852 (RMB 276,900 + RMB 24,425,652 + RMB 9,596,000 + RMB 3,044,300).

3. Regarding the issue of interest

Based on the facts established in this case, on July 28, 2009, Company A and Mining A signed the "Letter of Intent for Compensation for Overlaying Mining Rights in the Proposed Zhangjiakou-Tangshan Railway," which stated: "To ensure the implementation of the national key project, the mining rights holder and the construction entity have, through friendly negotiation, agreed to overlay the mining rights. Both parties agree that after the project is formally approved, based on the report on the evaluation of overlain mineral resources approved by the Provincial Department of Land and Resources, national policies, and relevant regulations, the parties shall negotiate and sign a compensation agreement." However, the parties failed to reach an agreement on the standard and amount of overlaying compensation. Based on the actual circumstances of this case, the first-instance court found that Mining A objectively suffered a loss of capital interest. Considering the principle of fairness, the court, in its discretion, ordered that interest on the compensation be paid from the date of filing of this lawsuit, i.e., January 17, 2017, at the same-period loan interest rate of the People's Bank of China (or the same-period loan prime rate published by the National Interbank Funding Center). This is not improper, and this Court upholds it. Company A and Company B argued on appeal that the failure of Mining A to receive compensation to date was due to its own fault and that the claim for interest should not be supported. These arguments lack sufficient evidentiary support and cannot stand.

(III) Regarding whether Company B should jointly bear the liability to pay the overlaying compensation with Company A

According to Article 33 of the Mineral Resources Law of the People's Republic of China and Article 4 of former Ministry of Land and Resources Document No. 137, the approval procedures for overlaying mineral resources shall be applied for by the construction entity, and the related overlaying compensation matters shall also be handled by the construction entity. In this case, the overlaying approval for the Zhangjiakou-Tangshan Railway project was handled by the construction entity, Company A, which submitted the "Application for Overlaying Mineral Resources for the Land Used in the New Zhangjiakou-Tangshan Railway Construction Project" and the "Investigation and Evaluation Report on Overlaying Mineral Resources for the Land Used in the New Zhangjiakou-Tangshan Railway Construction Project" to the natural resources authority, and signed the "Letter of Intent for Compensation for Overlaying Mining Rights in the Proposed Zhang-Tang Railway" with Mining A. The former Hebei Provincial Department of Land and Resources, after evaluation, approved the overlaying of identified important minerals and some construction non-metallic minerals within the scope of the construction project and issued the "Reply on the Overlaying of Mineral Resources for the 'New Zhangjiakou-Tangshan Railway Construction Project'," recommending that the construction entity properly handle the compensation relationship with the mining rights holder and proceed with the registration of the overlain mineral resource reserves as required. Accordingly, as the construction entity for the Zhang-Tang Railway in this case, Company A shall bear the overlaying compensation liability to the overlain mining rights holder in accordance with law.

Regarding whether Company B, as the entrusted construction agent, bears the overlaying compensation liability, this Court has already clearly stated in the civil judgment (2019) Supreme People's Court Civil Final No. 1793: "Regarding the issue of whether the construction agent bears compensation liability. If the overlain mining rights holder only sues the construction agent and does not simultaneously sue the construction entity, based on the protection of the mining rights holder's legitimate rights and interests, the specific circumstances of the case and the mining rights holder's claims may be considered to determine whether the construction agent is a proper subject of liability. If the construction agent needs to bear the overlaying compensation liability, it may, after bearing the liability to the mining rights holder, seek recovery from the construction entity or determine the internal allocation of liability based on the entrustment contract or other agreements signed with the construction entity. Therefore, in a case where both the construction entity and the construction agent are sued as parties, the first-instance judgment's determination that Construction Company A shall bear the overlaying compensation liability for the mining right in this case, and that Company B, the Zhang-Tang Project Department, and the Chengde Headquarters shall not bear liability, has corresponding factual and legal basis and is not improper." Accordingly, when a mining rights holder simultaneously sues both the construction entity and the construction agent for overlaying compensation liability, absent evidence that the construction agent knew or should have known that the entrusted matter was unlawful but still proceeded, or that the construction entity knew or should have known the construction agent's act was unlawful but failed to object, it is legally well-founded for the principal construction entity to bear the overlaying compensation liability and for the entrusted construction agent not to bear liability, which is also consistent with the general principles of agency. In this case, the Zhangjiakou-Tangshan Railway, a major national construction project approved by the National Development and Reform Commission, had its overlaying of mineral resources lawfully approved by the natural resources authority; it is not an illegal overlaying. Thus, there is no factual basis for Company B, as the construction agent, to have engaged in an unlawful entrustment and to bear joint or common liability with Company A. Company B's undertaking of construction management for the Zhang-Tang Railway project and its responsibility for disbursing compensation to the overlain enterprises are all lawful entrusted tasks. The first-instance judgment's determination that Company B should bear the overlaying compensation liability jointly with Company A lacks factual and legal basis and should be corrected. Company B's appeal that it is not the subject of the overlaying compensation liability and should not bear compensation liability jointly with Company A has corresponding basis and should be supported.

As to whether Wang should be joined in this lawsuit. Based on the undisputed facts confirmed by all parties, Mining A is an individually-owned business with Guo as the actual operator. After consolidation, the mining area of Mining A includes the original Mining A operated by Guo, the Guochengcheng Mine operated by Wang, and other unlicensed mines. The Guochengcheng Mine operated by Wang had a mining right certificate before consolidation, which became invalid after consolidation. Within the consolidated area, only Mining A holds a mining right certificate; the other mines do not. In May 2017, Wang applied to join the lawsuit as a rights holder. The first-instance court (Zunhua City People's Court) held that the mine in question had already been consolidated, Wang was not a necessary party to the lawsuit nor a third party in this case, and Wang should seek to assert his rights separately based on the agreements signed with Guo and others, and thus dismissed Wang's application. On January 8, 2018, Guo and Wang entered into a "Protocol" stipulating the distribution of compensation in this case. On February 28, 2022, because Mining A had not been in operation for a long time, the local administration for industry and commerce cancelled Mining A's registration. Subsequently, Guo applied to continue participating in the lawsuit as the plaintiff, and the first-instance judgment confirmed this, which has corresponding basis, and Company A has no objection to Guo's standing as plaintiff or to the absence of Wang's joinder in this lawsuit. Therefore, Company B's appeal ground that Wang should be joined in this lawsuit cannot stand.

Regarding the case acceptance fee in this case. Given that the case acceptance fee of RMB 1,509,839 stated in the first-instance judgment and the second-instance case acceptance fee of RMB 613,565 prepaid by Company A were both calculated without considering the corresponding interest claims, this Court hereby adjusts and reasonably determines the shares to be borne by each party. As to the adjustment of the appeal fee after Company A changed its appeal requests, Company A proposed that the appeal fees prepaid by both Company A and Company B should be considered together for supplementary payment and refund. Company B and Guo have no objection to this, and this Court confirms it.

In summary, the appeal requests of Company A and Company B are partially sustained. The first-instance judgment contains errors in the finding of some facts and in the application of law, and should be corrected. Pursuant to paragraph 1(2) of Article 177 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the judgment is as follows:

1. Set aside the civil judgment (2022) Ji Min Chu No. 6 of the Hebei High People's Court;

2. Company A shall, within thirty days from the effective date of this judgment, pay compensation of RMB 37,342,852 to Guo, plus interest calculated from January 17, 2017, to August 19, 2019, at the same-period loan interest rate of the People's Bank of China, and from August 20, 2019, to the date of actual payment, at the same-period loan prime rate published by the National Interbank Funding Center;

3. Dismiss the other claims of Guo.

If the obligation to pay money is not fulfilled within the period specified in this judgment, interest on the debt for the period of delayed performance shall be doubled in accordance with Article 264 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China.

The first-instance case acceptance fee is RMB 1,727,945 (RMB 1,509,839 prepaid by Guo), of which Guo shall bear RMB 1,449,967 and Company A shall bear RMB 277,978. The second-instance case acceptance fee is RMB 1,074,419 (RMB 613,565 prepaid by Company A), of which Company A shall bear RMB 253,259 and Guo shall bear RMB 821,160. The second-instance case acceptance fee of RMB 877,695.63 prepaid by Company B shall be refunded.

This judgment is final.
